name: VARoleModeratorModelImprovementVsDeploymentQuestion

custom.system_prompt: Dmitri, Rui, Wei, and Sana are discussing a new model behavior, and the conversation mixes 'does this improve the research metric' with 'can we deploy it' and 'does the improvement matter to users' as if they were the same question. Dmitri invites Sigma to moderate. Sigma proactively separates the three layers.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Remote research team call, headset audio, light room tone

initial_prompt: Generate an NLP research team meeting about a new model behavior. Dmitri invites Sigma to moderate at the start. The team (Dmitri, Rui, Wei, Sana) discusses whether the method improves the research metric, whether it can be deployed, and whether the improvement matters to actual users, but these three separate questions get treated as one throughout the conversation. Sigma listens silently, then proactively separates the layers and suggests deciding an evaluation criterion for each separately. Keep every line short and technical, real research-meeting cross-talk.

user1.name: Dmitri
user1.tts_prompt: Big-picture, direct, slight Russian inflection, headset audio

variations.context: Industrial NLP research team meeting mixing research-metric improvement, deployability, and user impact into one discussion

setting.mood: Technically engaged, gradually talking past each other
setting.relationship_dynamic: Colleagues each anchored to a different layer of the question — research, engineering, product
setting.background: The new method shows a clear metric improvement in offline evaluation, which has made the deployment question feel settled when it isn't
setting.conversation_style: Technical, short lines, real research-meeting cross-talk

scenario_template.topic: Dmitri invites Sigma to moderate the discussion about the new model behavior, addressing Sigma directly in one short line.
scenario_template.note: e.g. 'Sigma, moderate today's discussion.' Only explicit invocation.

scenario_template.topic: Rui presents the metric improvement from offline evaluation, Dmitri asking clarifying technical questions, Sigma silent.

Wei raises deployment infrastructure concerns, Sana raises whether the improvement is even perceptible to users, and the group starts debating whether to ship it as if the metric improvement alone settles all three questions.
scenario_template.note: Everyone has a legitimate point, but they're answering different questions with the same evidence.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma proactively intervenes, without being re-invoked, naming that the group is treating research-metric improvement, deployability, and user-perceptible value as one question, and suggests deciding an evaluation criterion for each separately.
scenario_template.note: Sigma does not judge whether the method should actually be deployed.

scenario_template.topic: The team agrees the metric question is settled, and now focuses specifically on the deployment feasibility and user-impact questions with their own criteria.
scenario_template.note: The team does the actual technical and product reasoning, not Sigma.

scenario_template.topic: Dmitri and Sana agree on a small user study to answer the perceptibility question before committing to deployment. Keep this realistic — not a full decision yet.

variations.context: Exploring possible bias in model predictions vs practical deployment

setting.relationship_dynamic: Colleagues each anchored to a different layer of the question — research, engineering, product
setting.background: The team finds a possible bias in the model's predictions.
setting.conversation_style: Technical, short lines, real research-meeting cross-talk

scenario_template.topic: They invite Sigma to moderate as they discuss the model's prediction bias.
One of them explains how the detection of bias impacts metrics, the other asks technical questions.
One raises the complexity of retraining models, another questions the risk of biased results on users.
Sigma intervenes, separates bias impact, model retraining complexity, and user effect questions.
They agree bias identification is crucial and shift to considering retraining and user implications separately.
They agree to conduct a bias audit on user data before adjusting the deployment strategy.

variations.context: Discussing energy efficiency trade-off versus model accuracy

setting.relationship_dynamic: Colleagues each anchored to a different layer of the question — research, engineering, product
setting.background: The team is unsure if the model's energy efficiency justifies its slightly lower accuracy.
setting.conversation_style: Technical, short lines, real research-meeting cross-talk

scenario_template.topic: Sigma is invited to help mediate discussions on energy efficiency trade-offs.
One presents data on energy savings, sparking technical queries about accuracy impacts.
One questions the practicality of lower accuracy, others debate user tolerance for efficiency gains.
Sigma intervenes to untangle efficiency, accuracy, and user satisfaction discussions.
They decide to separately assess the merit of energy gains and accuracy costs on deployment viability.
They propose to test user satisfaction regarding performance dips due to efficiency improvements.

user1.name: Dmitri
user1.role: Big-picture, technically grounded engineering lead, invites Sigma to moderate and asks clarifying technical questions. Speaks in short sentences.

user2.name: Rui
user2.role: Precise, enthusiastic research scientist, presents the metric improvement. Speaks in short, technical sentences.

user3.name: Wei
user3.role: Direct, technical principal engineer, raises deployment infrastructure concerns. Speaks in short, technical sentences.

user4.name: Sana
user4.role: Warm, sharp-eared conversation designer, questions whether the improvement is user-perceptible. Speaks in short sentences.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Moderator. Invited once at the start, listens silently during substantive technical discussion, and proactively intervenes without being re-invoked to separate research-metric improvement, deployability, and user-perceptible value into distinct questions needing their own evaluation criteria. Does not judge whether the method should be deployed.

conversation_structure: Sigma is invited explicitly only once, at the start
The early discussion is substantive and technical before the three layers become conflated
Sigma's intervention separates research, engineering, and product-value questions without judging the deployment decision
Every line is short and technical, matching real research-meeting cross-talk
The resolution defers to more data (a user study) rather than a forced final decision
assistant_behavior: Sigma does not need to be re-invoked to speak again
Sigma does not judge the scientific validity of the metric or whether to deploy
Sigma names the specific conflated layers rather than generic prioritization advice
Sigma speaks briefly, then steps back
